title: Delta radiomics for rectal cancer response prediction with hybrid 0.35 T magnetic resonance-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT): a hypothesis-generating study for an innovative personalized medicine approach

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Delta radiomics for rectal cancer response prediction with hybrid 0.35 T magnetic resonance-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT): a hypothesis-generating study for an innovative personalized medicine approach》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · Par4】Conservative surgical approaches have recently been investigated in patients showing clinical complete response (cCR) after neoadjuvant treatments: both local excision (LE) and “watch and wait” (W&W) approaches represent to date feasible options in order to reduce morbidities and toxicities related to unnecessary TME procedures [7–9].

【Introduction · Par8】A few studies suggest models for pCR prediction in LARC founded on clinical data information or on features extracted from previously acquired diagnostic images (i.e. staging scans) or during RCT, but the evidence about cCR prediction is still poor. The extraction of these significant features from biomedical images takes advantage of innovative biotechnologies, such as the radiomics analysis techniques that aim to a quantitative analysis of the images [17–19].

evidence.text: Conservative surgical approaches have recently been investigated in patients showing clinical complete response (cCR) after neoadjuvant treatments: both local excision (LE) and “watch and wait” (W&W) approaches represent to date feasible options in order to reduce morbidities and toxicities related to unnecessary TME procedures [7–9].

A few studies suggest models for pCR prediction in LARC founded on clinical data information or on features extracted from previously acquired diagnostic images (i.e. staging scans) or during RCT, but the evidence about cCR prediction is still poor. The extraction of these significant features from biomedical images takes advantage of innovative biotechnologies, such as the radiomics analysis techniques that aim to a quantitative analysis of the images [17–19].

【Patients selection criteria · Par16】Patients affected by locally advanced (cT2-4 and/or cN0-1, cM0) rectal adenocarcinoma, undergoing long-course neoadjuvant RCT with a low-Tesla tri-Co-60 MRI-Hybrid system have been enrolled for this study.

【Patients selection criteria · Par17】Specific informed consent and MRI safety screening forms were administered to all eligible patients.

evidence.text: Patients affected by locally advanced (cT2-4 and/or cN0-1, cM0) rectal adenocarcinoma, undergoing long-course neoadjuvant RCT with a low-Tesla tri-Co-60 MRI-Hybrid system have been enrolled for this study.
Specific informed consent and MRI safety screening forms were administered to all eligible patients.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Delta radiomics for rectal cancer response prediction with hybrid 0.35 T magnetic resonance-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT): a hypothesis-generating study for an innovative personalized medicine approach》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · Par45】Sixteen consecutive patients (13 males and 3 females) affected by LARC (stages IIA–IIIC), with a median age of 64 years (range 49–86) were retrospectively enrolled for this study.

【Results · Par46】Five patients (31%) showed cCR at restaging examinations (DRE and MRI).
